chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from more than one, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'The first thing Allah — Mighty is His mention — will question the servant about is that He will say to him: Did I not quench you from the fresh waters of the Euphrates?'

key_terms.أُرْوِكَ: From the root ر-و-ي, meaning to give to drink until sated/quenched — indicating full satisfaction rather than partial refreshment
key_terms.جَلَّ ذِكْرُهُ: A formula of glorification of God, meaning 'Mighty is His mention' — an honorific used for God in classical Shia hadith literature
key_terms.عَذْبُ الْفُرَاتِ: The sweet/fresh water of the Euphrates — used here as the prime symbol of God's blessing of fresh water

ai.seo_question: What is the first question God will ask the servant on the Day of Judgment according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes an eschatological scene where God's first question to His servant on the Day of Judgment concerns the blessing of fresh water — specifically the Euphrates. This teaching frames divine accountability around gratitude for elemental blessings, reminding believers that even the most basic bounties (water) will be subject to reckoning. The Euphrates, as the most prominent river of the Islamic world at the time, served as the paradigmatic example of divine provision of water.
